A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pearl mouse is a model for Hermannsky-Pudlak syndrome, a human disease characterized by oculocutaneous albinism, platelet storage pool deficiency, and pulmonary fibrosis.

the pearl mouse is a model for the Hermansky-Putlak syndrome (HPS) in which the beta3A subunits of the AP- 3 adaptor complex is mutated and this leads to the accumulation of melanosomes, lysosomes and platelets in the pearl mutant.

the beta3A subunits of the AP- 3 adaptor complex are essential for normal pigmentation and platelet function in the mouse, and that defects in the AP-3 subunit genes are a cause of Hermansky-Puddlak syndrome in humans.
